title: The Relate playground: an agent's memory, in your browser
description: A chat on one side, the agent's memory on the other. As the conversation goes on, the agent writes what it learns into Relate 1.2.0, compiled to WebAssembly, and the memory grows as a graph in front of you, drawn with NVL. When it is asked something in a later session, one statement combines vector search, full-text search and graph hops, and the page highlights the paths that statement returned. The agent's words are scripted; every read and write of its memory is a real statement, run in the tab under a graph type that refuses a malformed memory. Three conversations to play, then ask your own questions.
browser: Runs in any current browser with module workers and WebAssembly. There is no model to download: the page is 9 MB (about 3 MB as the server compresses it), most of it the database.
credits: Relate 1.2.0 WebAssembly build (Apache-2.0), served here as a pinned copy of npm's @relate/relate-wasm 1.2.0.

The memory model (messages, entities, memories that supersede one another) and the shape of the recall statement follow Relate's own cookbook recipes on agent memory and hybrid recall (relatedb.ai/cookbook, Apache-2.0); the statements, conversations and page are this repository's.
